label: Institution
name: Masjid Al-Amin
summary:
Masjid Al-Amin (Arabic: مسجد الأمين, Mosque of the Trustworthy — a title of the Prophet Muhammad) is a significant mosque in Singapore serving the Bedok North area of the island's eastern region, one of the larger mosques in Singapore's MUIS-administered network of approximately 70 mosques. The mosque serves the Malay-Muslim community of Bedok, one of Singapore's most densely populated residential areas and home to a significant Muslim population.

The name 'Al-Amin' (the Trustworthy) was a honorific given to the Prophet Muhammad before he received his prophetic mission — acknowledging his reputation for integrity and reliability among his Meccan community before 610 CE. This pre-prophetic title reflects a tradition of naming mosques after attributes or titles that evoke the Prophet's character and moral qualities.

Bedok's demographic composition — with a significant Malay-Muslim community in a predominantly HDB (Housing Development Board) public housing estate — reflects Singapore's pattern of ethnic integration through public housing: Singapore's HDB policy deliberately mixes ethnic groups within housing estates, but Malay-Muslim families have naturally clustered somewhat more in certain areas. Masjid Al-Amin serves as the community's religious and social anchor in Bedok's dense residential environment.
